newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian tycoon seeks top political job.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian tycoon seeks top political job.

text.p: Joseph Chong, head of Westmont Holdings Sdn Bhd, will challenge for the presidency of Malaysia's Gerakan party, a member of the ruling National Front coalition, the Bernama news agency said on Thursday.
It said Chong, 48, elected to parliament in last year's general election, submitted his papers as a presidential candidate in the Gerakan party polls on October 5.

He will formally announce his challenge to Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik for the presidency and introduce other members of his "vision team" at a news conference on Friday, after he returns from Manila, it said.

Chong is managing director of Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd, which has a controlling stake in National Steel of the Philippines. He also controls property-based Westmont Land (Asia) Bhd and Westmont Industries Bhd

The Gerakan party controls northern Penang state, known as Malaysia's Silicon Valley because of the many large electronics companies on the island. The mostly Chinese party is also one of several race-based groups that make up Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's multi-racial National Front.
Lim and Chong have accused each other of encouraging "money politics," or vote buying. Both vehemently deny the allegations.
Lim also accused Chong of undermining confidence in the party leadership by forming his "vision team" to challenge the top posts in Gerakan's elections.
On Sunday, Lim warned that Chong may be expelled if he continues to make verbal attacks against the party.
Gerakan's October internal elections on October 5 are scheduled a few days ahead of party polls in Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation.
